name: Justin Trudeau
role: Prime Minister of Canada (2015–2025); Liberal Party leader (2013–2025)
summary: Liberal leader who governed Canada for nearly a decade with a socially progressive, fiscally expansionary record: carbon pricing, cannabis legalization, medical assistance in dying, a national child benefit and child care system, dental care and an early pharmacare phase. He also backed oil pipelines, assault-style weapon bans, the Emergencies Act in 2022 and, late in his tenure, lower immigration levels.

sources.title: Further strengthening our gun control laws (Bill C-21)
sources.author: Prime Minister's Office

universal-healthcare.rationale: Stated commitment to the 'universal, public health care system' and delivered a dental care plan and the first phase of national pharmacare.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: His government raised taxes on the top one percent while cutting middle-class taxes, and the 2021 platform said the wealthiest and big banks should pay more; no claim of a 'significant' further rise.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Government required large tech platforms to pay for news and priced pollution, and he said profitable corporations must contribute; this is a record on specific sectors, not a general statement.

cut-welfare.rationale: Record of expanding benefits (Canada Child Benefit, dental, pharmacare); he did not address the dependency argument directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: His government legalized recreational cannabis (2018); no position found on other recreational drugs, so limited to cannabis.

limit-guns.rationale: Banned 1,500 assault-style firearm models by regulation in 2020 and froze handgun sales in Bill C-21, while stating most owners use guns responsibly.

empower-police-military.rationale: Increased defence funding (Our North, Strong and Free) and invoked the Emergencies Act to give police added tools in 2022.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Apologized for the historic persecution of LGBTQ2 Canadians and said everyone should be free to love who they love; no direct statement on marriage found, so medium.

abortion-legal.rationale: Stated the government will never put a woman's right to choose up for debate and called abortion a fundamental right.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Apologized for residential schools, committed to decolonizing laws and the TRC calls to action, and pledged to fight systemic racism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: In October 2024 announced cuts to immigration levels to pause population growth while also calling immigration vital; most recent position is to reduce levels.

free-trade.rationale: Pursued trade deals (CUSMA, CETA, CPTPP) and pledged with China's premier to promote free trade and multilateralism; did not claim it benefits everyone.

open-borders.rationale: Said immigration 'must be controlled' and sustainable; no direct statement on eventual open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Rejected the idea that what is good for the economy is bad for the environment and pursued growth alongside climate policy.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Priced carbon, legislated net zero by 2050 and called climate action a moral and economic imperative, while also approving pipelines.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Committed to implementing UNDRIP and a nation-to-nation relationship; no direct statement on land authority.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Mandate letters call for performance measurement, evidence and results; he did not frame it against ideology.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Backs Israel's right to defend itself and a two-state solution with a secure Israel beside a Palestinian state; no direct statement on a Jewish state's right.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Ran deficits to fund infrastructure, family benefits and pandemic support, stating 'this is not the time for austerity'.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Appointed Canada's first gender-balanced cabinet and advocates gender equality; no statement on legal gender roles.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Approved and later bought the Trans Mountain expansion to reach foreign markets, while also proposing emissions limits and a carbon price.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Said diversity is a source of strength and not a difficulty to be overcome.

proportional-representation.rationale: Dropped electoral reform, saying proportional voting would be too divisive, and preferred ranked ballots.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Apology and diversity speeches affirm equal rights and dignity regardless of sexual orientation, origin or religion.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Said Canada came into being without those who were there first and pledged to decolonize its laws; he did not call it a colonial project generally.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Said Canada is stronger and more successful because of its diversity.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Record: invoked the Emergencies Act in February 2022 against the trucker convoy, freezing protesters' bank accounts; a federal court later ruled the use unreasonable.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Maintained NATO membership and NORAD modernization.

minority-language-support.rationale: Committed to an Indigenous Languages Act and raised francophone immigration targets outside Quebec.

collective-defense.rationale: Calls NATO a cornerstone of transatlantic security and increased Canada's contribution; Article 5 not stated explicitly.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Called Russian-held regions of Ukraine illegally occupied and the annexation referendums illegitimate; the Crimea statement calls the occupation illegal.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Cut taxes for the middle class and raised the top rate.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Appointed a gender-balanced cabinet as a choice; no requirement for public bodies recorded.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Amended the Canadian Human Rights Act to protect gender identity and expression, and criminalized conversion therapy.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Said the Emergencies Act measures must comply with the Charter and that the Act exists to uphold it.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Mandate letters say government and its information should be open by default.

treaties-binding.rationale: Said early treaties had not been fully honoured or implemented and pursued a nation-to-nation relationship.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Refers to the Holocaust as historical fact and condemns Hamas's 7 October attack as the deadliest on Jewish people since then.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Apologized in 2017 for past criminalization and banned conversion therapy.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: 2017 law added gender identity and expression to the Human Rights Act and Criminal Code.

assisted-dying.rationale: His government passed the 2016 medical assistance in dying law.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Said he deeply disagrees with Bill 21 and that no one should lose their job because of religion.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Raised defence spending and committed to 2% of GDP by 2032.

open-government-data.rationale: Mandate letter sets openness by default; no statement on publishing citizen proposals.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Apology condemned the military purge of LGBTQ2 members as prejudiced and wrong.

second-chamber.rationale: Kept the Senate and reformed its appointment process rather than abolishing it.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Introduced federal carbon pollution pricing, calling it the best way to tackle climate change.

future-generations.rationale: Repeatedly framed climate and pipeline policy as leaving a cleaner environment for children.

close-ties-china.rationale: Sought a strengthened partnership with China in 2018, after which relations soured over detained Canadians.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Mandate letter says to give more help to those who need it and less to those who do not, yet his government also built universal programs.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Platform and speeches commit to fighting systemic racism, implying continuing barriers.

notes: Living person: answers rest only on his own statements and his government's record. Immigration moved from expansion to reduction in 2024 and the most recent position was used. Several topics could not be sourced from pages opened here (2015 and 2019 platforms, the full 2021 platform, Common Ground, Hansard, mandate letters beyond Finance and Health), so those statements are null.
